response.consequence: The test most likely fails, or it only passes because some of those abilities are absent in the mocked setup. If it passes for that reason, it doesn't check the menu content it claims to check.
response.explanation: The test grants Update and Delete permissions (beforeEach) and then asserts that the menu has exactly 4 items. AlertRuleMenu also renders a Pause item for Grafana rules when canPause, which comes from Update, and a Delete item when canDelete is true and a ruler rule exists. The test defines ui.menuItems.delete but never uses it. With the granted permissions the menu would show Pause, Silence, Duplicate, Copy link, Export and Delete, so `byRole('menuitem').getAll().length` is not 4. The comment's "all 4 menu actions" ignores Pause and Delete.
response.title: Menu test asserts exactly 4 items although permissions yield more (pause, delete)

response.consequence: In the rule list, users cannot pause or export Grafana-managed recording rules from the menu. They could do so before, when abilities came from the ruler rule. This is a UI behavior regression only. No unauthorized action becomes possible, because permission checks still apply.
response.explanation: The ruler-based abilities gate Pause, Restore, DeletePermanently and ModifyExport on `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)`, which is true for all Grafana-managed rules, recording rules included. The new `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` gates the same actions on `prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)`. A Grafana recording rule therefore gets `supported=false` for these actions. Silence is the only action that should be restricted to alerting rules. AlertRuleMenu now takes its abilities from this hook when it is given a promRule, as the list view does. A recording rule's menu in the list view therefore loses Pause and Export, which are available through the ruler path.
response.title: Prom-rule abilities disable Pause, Export, Restore and DeletePermanently for Grafana recording rules

response.consequence: For federated Mimir rule groups, the UI offers edit and delete actions that were previously hidden. Users are shown actions that should be disallowed for federated rules, and the other federated-rule checks are bypassed.
response.explanation: The old useAllAlertRuleAbilities set isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group), which makes rules in cross-tenant federated groups (group.source_tenants is an array) immutable. The change delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities, where isFederated is hardcoded to false (the check is commented out). So a CombinedRule from a federated group now reports Update, Delete, Pause, Restore and DeletePermanently as supported. Other code, such as RuleViewer and RuleDetailsButtons, still treats these groups as federated.
response.title: Federated rule groups no longer blocked from edit/delete in useAllAlertRuleAbilities

response.explanation: The new mocks match the hooks that AlertRuleMenu actually calls (useRulerRuleAbilities and useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities) and the one RuleActionsButtons calls (useAlertRuleAbility). The default mocks deny every ability. For Grafana rules the ruler abilities therefore stay false and the Grafana prom abilities decide the result. For cloud rules the Grafana prom hook gets skipToken and the default deny applies. The negative and positive assertions can both fail as written.
